C-^ inside a search pushes the same prompt over the search line (outside a search C-^ keeps its vim c_CTRL-^ meaning)

arms the input method for exactly one character (dispatches to :activate-transient-input-method, which swaps the method's table in, bypasses the 'imsearch' switch for one lookup and turns itself off again). The C-x \ key inside a search prompt was already wired to the same one-character translation
resumes a spell check that was interrupted, starting from the word at point, and refuses when the current buffer is not the one the halted session belongs to

calls spell::kill_ispell — invalidates the loaded dictionary cache and clears the session-only accept lists (the file-backed personal dictionary is left alone, since a restarted Ispell re-reads it) — and drops any halted ispell-region session with it

:kbd C-x C-f [register] parses an Emacs key description (C-/M-/S- prefixes, <TAB>/RET/SPC/DEL/ESC/arrow names) into zmax's key-sequence notation, validates it with zmax_view::input::parse_macro and writes it to a register, where @{reg} replays it; an unparsable description is an error rather than a silent no-op

during macro *execution* it stops the replay where it is: replay_macro now feeds keys through run_macro_keys, which parks the rest of the repetition plus the remaining repetitions when a query is raised. The answer keys are the manual's — SPC/y continue, DEL/n skip the rest of this repetition and start the next, RET/q cancel the remaining repetitions, C-r enter a recursive edit (C-M-c out of it asks again). While a macro is being defined the key only records itself
errors with `Not defining or executing keyboard macro` unless a macro is running or being defined, and requests a redraw only while one is executing — the two branches of kmacro.el's body

makes the prompt's default — the value it runs when the line is left empty — the completion candidate; the C-x DOWN key in the prompt already ran the same Prompt::complete_from_default, this exposes it by name

prompts for a file, truncates it and records from then on: Application::render appends every painted screen (cell text, one form feed per frame) to it, until the command is run again with an empty name, which closes the script
opens the command picker with the working directory bound to the project root, so the next command you choose runs in the project
:serial-term <port> [speed] [line] opens a terminal on the serial device through the first available of picocom/screen/cu/minicom, defaulting to 9600 bps
sends SIGQUIT to the running TeX subprocess (what Emacs's quit-process does) and errors when none is running; C-c C-k in a LaTeX buffer now runs it

`?` in a completing read (any prompt that is not the `:` line, a search or the `=` expression line — Prompt::is_completing_read) recomputes and shows the candidate list, and says `No completions` when there are none
C-c C-c in C/C++ buffers runs comment-region: it inserts the line comment token at the first non-blank of every line the region covers, mark active or not
edit-abbrevs now puts the major mode `edit-abbrevs` on the buffer it opens, and that mode binds C-c C-c to define-abbrevs — which redefines the abbrevs from the text in the buffer

edit-tab-stops now opens Emacs's ruler buffer (a colon at every stop over the tens/units rulers and the `To install changes, type C-c C-c` line) in major mode edit-tab-stops; C-c C-c reads the colon columns off the first line and installs them as the tab stops
C-c C-k in a LaTeX buffer kills the running TeX subprocess with SIGQUIT (tex-kill-job)
C-c [ in an Org buffer runs org-agenda-file-to-front, which adds the current file to the front of the agenda file list

isearch-abort in two stages, as the manual describes: a failing search rubs back to the characters that last matched and stays in the search, a successful one goes back to where the search started and quits — so C-g C-g is what leaves a failing search (Prompt::isearch_abort)
C-h is the isearch help prefix; C-h C-h (and C-h ?, C-h F1) shows the isearch-help-map options, with b/k/m/q for describe-bindings, describe-key, describe-mode and quit
C-M-c leaves the innermost recursive editing level; with a kbd-macro-query C-r level it resumes by asking the query again

the first C-SPC pushes point onto the mark ring (emacs_mark::push) and activates it, the second — recognised by set_mark_command as a repeat at the same point in the same buffer — deactivates it, so the pair leaves the mark on the ring without an active region, which is what the Mark Ring node documents

undo with a universal argument is selective undo: it walks the document history back until the region's text differs, winds the history forward again so nothing outside the region moves, and puts just the region back to the older text — the effect of undoing the most recent change inside the region

C-c C-w reads the universal argument: without one it is fortran-window-create-momentarily (the column-72 marker is taken down by the next key), with one it is fortran-window-create — the marker stays up and you carry on editing with it

the command adds a character to the search string by name and is reachable by name during a search, but zmax's table is the digraph table rather than a Unicode-name database (so `a:` not `LATIN SMALL LETTER A WITH DIAERESIS`), and the C-x 8 RET key sequence itself is not wired into the search prompt — C-x in the prompt is the minibuffer completion prefix, and `8` is not a key under it
same as C-x 8 RET: the command exists and appends by mnemonic, but there is no emoji-name database behind it and the C-x 8 e RET key sequence is not wired into the search prompt

inside a search C-^ pushes the input-method prompt (isearch-toggle-specified-input-method): pick one of the installed keymap/{name}.vim methods and the search string is typed through it. Outside a search the key keeps vim's c_CTRL-^ ('imsearch' toggle)

M-DOWN in the minibuffer moves to the next completion candidate and puts it on the line (minibuffer-completion-auto-choose defaults to t, which is what selecting does here); with no candidates it says so
M-UP is the backward mirror of M-DOWN: previous candidate, inserted on the line
M-RET takes the candidate the list is on (the first when none is selected), splices it into the line and accepts the minibuffer with it

isearch-edit-string: the search stops running on every keystroke and the buffer stays on the match it is on while the string is edited; RET resumes the incremental search with the edited string (Prompt::isearch_edit_string and the RET arm guarded by isearch_edit)
isearch-yank-pop: after C-y appended the current kill, M-y replaces that appended text with the next-older kill, tracking how much the last yank added (Prompt::isearch_yank_pop / isearch_yank_len)

M-g is a prefix in the *xref* overlay: M-g M-n (and M-g n) is next-error — it moves to the next hit and shows it, opening the file and putting point on the match in the buffer underneath while the results list stays up
M-g M-p (and M-g p) is previous-error in the *xref* overlay: previous hit, shown the same way

SPC in a completing read runs Prompt::complete_word — it completes to the longest common prefix but stops at the first word separator past what is typed, so a second SPC completes the next word. Emacs does not bind this where the argument may contain spaces; here the same rule is Prompt::is_completing_read (not the `:` line, not a search, not the `=` line), and a space that completes nothing is inserted as a space

lax space matching is on by default (IsearchFlags::lax_whitespace), so a space typed into a search matches any run of spaces and tabs — `foo bar` finds `foo  bar` — via zmax_core::search::lax_whitespace_regexp; M-s SPC (isearch-toggle-lax-whitespace) turns it off and back on

toggles a flag in zmax-view::graphics that both terminal backends read when they emit DECSCUSR, so the cursor switches between the steady and the blinking value of whatever shape :set cursorshape selected; takes an optional 1/0/on/off argument

scans the visible lines with zmax_core::bug_reference and paints each Bug#1234 / tracker reference with the markup.link.url face; the reference under the cursor is followed by open_url_under_cursor, which expands :bug-reference-url-format's %s with the reference number
same scan as bug-reference-mode, then the matches are filtered to those inside a comment or string span (the same comment_string_spans_in the flyspell-prog-mode path uses)

sets the buffer's major mode to change-log and its indent style to tabs (emacs derives the mode from Text mode and sets indent-tabs-mode t / tab-width 8); the add-log commands that the mode exists for -- change-log-goto-source, change-log-merge, add-change-log-entry -- are separate commands that work in that buffer

completes the partial word before point from the spelling dictionary (emacs text-mode-ispell-word-completion): candidates come from spell::words_with_prefix, i.e. the loaded :spelllang wordlist plus words added with :spellgood, and are offered through the same picker as the vim i_CTRL-X completions; capped at 200 candidates

buffer-local toggle; when on, the completion handler puts the top candidate's suffix after point as ghost text instead of opening the menu, honouring completion-preview-minimum-symbol-length (3) and completion-preview-exact-match-only
the same inline preview for every buffer; buffers whose local completion-preview-mode was toggled keep their own setting, as in emacs

swaps the live keymap to the `cua` preset (the emacs preset plus a CUA overlay) and restores the displaced preset when turned off: C-x cuts and C-c copies while a region is live, C-v pastes and C-z undoes unconditionally, C-RET starts a rectangle, shifted motions start/extend a region. The manual's escape back to the prefix maps is the S-C-x chord; the other escape it lists (typing C-x twice within cua-prefix-override-inhibit-delay) is a timer, not a chord, and is not implemented

turns bug-reference highlighting on for the buffer and points bug-reference-url-format at https://debbugs.gnu.org/cgi/bugreport.cgi?bug=%s, so Bug#1234 is linkified and following it opens the debbugs bug page; turning the mode off drops the highlighting again

while on, a mouse-move over a word runs an RFC 2229 DICT lookup (dictionary-server, dict.org:2628 by default, settable as an argument) on a blocking task and shows the definitions in a popup -- the terminal frame's tooltip; the same word under the pointer is not re-queried, and a 552 no-match is reported on the status line
icomplete display plus the ido flavouring: RET takes the top candidate rather than the literal input (icomplete-fido-ret). Aliased :fido-vertical-mode for the vertical display

the matching candidates are rendered on the prompt line itself as {a | b | c} while typing, through a port of icomplete-completions honouring icomplete-separator, icomplete-prospects-height and icomplete-hide-common-prefix
the same candidates one per line; turning it on turns icomplete-mode on when neither it nor fido-mode is already on, as icomplete.el does

buffer-local; turning it on snapshots the rope and the renderer diffs the snapshot against the live text, painting inserted runs and -- like hilit-chg-delete -- the single character that took a deletion's place; the baseline is re-based on each save. Emacs' extra commands (highlight-changes-next-change, -rotate-faces, -remove-highlight) are not part of this item and are not implemented
a prompt opened while another is still on the compositor stack renders a [N] depth prefix before its prompt string; the depth is how many prompt layers are live
the prompt's (default X) segment is rendered only while the input is still the empty one the prompt opened with, and disappears as soon as it is typed over

runs the major-mode command in the current buffer -- sets its major mode to minibuffer-inactive, which the mode line shows and the major-mode keymap overlay keys off. What is NOT ported: zmax's minibuffer is an ephemeral compositor prompt layer, not a persistent buffer, so there is no inactive-minibuffer buffer for the mode to be the default major mode of

prompts for the technique with the same completion set and `banish` default as emacs and records it; `none` turns the mode off. What is NOT ported: nothing warps -- a terminal application cannot move the host's mouse pointer, so there is no visible effect, exactly as in emacs -nw

with the mode on (the default) <backspace> erases backwards and <delete> forwards; turning it off swaps the two key events before the keymap is consulted, which is the remedy the manual's DEL Does Not Delete node prescribes. Takes an optional 1/0/on/off argument
buffer-local; while on, RET at the end of a line opening one of nroff-brace-table's requests (.(b, .DS, .FS, .KS, ...) inserts the matching closing request below, ported from nroff-electric-newline

an indented line that carries text starts a paragraph, so paragraph motion works on prose separated by indentation rather than blank lines; paragraph-separate is left alone, so a whitespace-only line still separates rather than starts
text-mode plus that paragraph rule, which is all the major mode adds: it clears the buffer's language and turns the indent-starts-a-paragraph rule on

after a command bound to a chord of two or more keys, that chord's last key alone runs it again -- C-x u then u u u, C-x o then o o o, C-x { then } ^ v. The transient map is the chord's own prefix node in the live keymap (zmax has no per-command repeat-map property), the accepted keys are echoed on the status line, RET is repeat-exit-key, and any other key ends the repetition and is then executed normally. repeat-exit-timeout is not implemented (emacs leaves it nil by default)

while on, show_text_in_scratch (shell output, describe-* reports, listings) opens the temporary buffer in its own horizontal split and resizes it to its line count instead of replacing the current window; the height is capped at half the frame, which is emacs' default temp-buffer-max-height

decides where help text lands: with the mode on (the default) an LSP hover opens the hover popup -- the terminal frame's tooltip -- and with it off the hover is echoed on the status line instead, which is emacs' 'shown in the echo area' branch

buffer-local; while on, the newlines inserted by RET (insert_newline) and o/O (open-line) get a `hard` text property, which sticks to the character through later edits via the existing text-props position mapping, and the fill commands (gq/gw/:reflow) cut the region at every hard newline and fill each piece separately, so a hard line break is never removed

a second C-SPC on the spot where the first one landed activates the mark and sets the temporary transient-mark flag, so the region is shaded for this one region even with transient-mark-mode off; pressing it again with the region already active deactivates the mark instead, and the temporary flag is cleared by deactivate-mark

Control + a left press in the editor body opens the buffer menu (the buffer picker) through mouse_buffer_menu, as emacs's C-down-mouse-1 does. Under the vim/spacemacs presets the chord keeps vim's <C-LeftMouse> go-to-tag meaning, so this is the emacs/default preset behaviour.

Control + a middle press opens the Text Properties menu (faces and colors) through facemenu, which is what facemenu.el binds C-down-mouse-2 to; the matching release is consumed so it does not also paste. Non-vim presets only, where the middle button is not vim's paste.

C-mouse-2 on a window's mode line splits that window into two side-by-side windows and then moves the new boundary to the clicked column (mouse-split-window-horizontally). The press and release must land on the same mode line. Previously this ran hsplit, which stacked the windows instead.
With the menu bar turned off, C-mouse-3 pops up the whole menu-bar tree (every menu, not just the mode-specific ones), which is what the emacs manual specifies for a hidden menu bar.

C-S-mouse-3 runs ffap_menu with the click position, which pops a menu of every file/URL mentioned in the buffer (ordered by position, deduplicated) at the pointer; choosing one sets the mark, jumps to that occurrence and visits it. Run from a key the same command offers the list as a picker.

After M-x ffap-bindings, C-x 4 f visits the file named at point in another window: an existing other window is reused, and only a sole window is split. The guess is read in the window point is in. With no file name at point the chord falls back to the ordinary find-file-other-window picker, matching emacs's ffap commands prompting when the guess is empty.
After M-x ffap-bindings, C-x 5 f makes a frame and visits the file named at point in it (ffap-other-frame); with nothing at point it stays the ordinary find-file-other-frame picker.

M-x ffap-bindings sets Editor::ffap_bindings, and file_picker (the command C-x C-f runs) then hands over to find-file-at-point — the same command remap emacs installs, so every key bound to find-file changes with it. Filenames, ~ expansion, URLs and a trailing :LINE are all recognised by the guesser; with nothing at point the picker opens as before.

C-x C-r now runs find-file-read-only (a new command: pick a file, and the buffer arrives with doc.readonly set) instead of the plain picker; with ffap-bindings installed it hands over to ffap-read-only, visiting the file named at point read-only.

After M-x ffap-bindings, C-x C-v visits the file named at point in place of this buffer and kills the buffer it replaced (find-alternate-file's distinguishing behaviour); a buffer with unsaved changes is kept and reported instead.
After M-x ffap-bindings, C-x d opens Dired on the file/directory name at point (dired-at-point) instead of on the workspace root; with nothing at point the ordinary Dired opens.
C-x t C-f is now bound (alongside C-x t f) to find-file-other-tab; with ffap-bindings installed it hands over to ffap-other-tab, which opens a new tab and visits the file named at point in it.

With context-menu-mode on, pressing the right button over text pops the context menu at the click through context-menu-open — the same command S-F10 runs. With the mode off nothing pops up, and under vim's mousemodel=extend the right button extends the region instead.

Alt + dragging the left button sets the secondary selection from the anchor M-mouse-1 dropped to the pointer, painting it with the secondary-selection face and leaving point and the primary region untouched. Non-vim presets only (Alt+click adds a cursor under vim/spacemacs).
Alt + a left press anchors the secondary selection at the click (clearing the previous one) instead of adding a cursor. Non-vim presets only.
Alt + a middle click inserts the secondary selection's text at the click; the secondary selection itself stays where it is. Non-vim presets only, where Alt+middle is not the register replace.

Alt + a right click copies the secondary selection to the mouse-yank register; a second click with the same text still saved deletes it. The Alt right *press* is consumed so no context menu opens over it. Non-vim presets only.

mouse-1 on a mode line selects the window it belongs to (mouse_select_window acts on Editor::last_mouse_view, the window the click named). On the mode line of a window that has one below it the press also starts a drag that moves the boundary, changing the heights above and below; the resize clamps at the minimum pane size and never deletes a window.

Clicking mouse-1 on the search prompt moves the prompt cursor to the clicked column and switches the running search into edit mode — RET resumes searching with the edited string (Prompt::isearch_edit_string in ui/prompt.rs). The static command of the same name is the M-e / M-x form of the same behaviour.
mouse-2 on a mode line expands that window to fill the frame (delete-other-windows). The press and release must land on the same mode line, and it runs ahead of the middle-click paste.

Middle-clicking the search prompt while a search is running appends the selection (the '+' register, the same text C-y takes) to the search string and re-runs the search; an empty clipboard reports so. Handled in the prompt's isearch (ui/prompt.rs); the static command of the same name is the M-x form.
mouse-3 on a mode line deletes the window it belongs to, and does nothing when it is the only window. The press and release must land on the same mode line.

S-F10 opens the context menu from the keyboard, anchored at point's screen cell (the click position is only used when the mouse opened it). Bound in the shipped spacemacs default's normal mode and in the emacs preset.

Shift + a middle click folds the block the click landed in, or unfolds it when it is already folded (zmax's folds are hideshow's blocks — the same fold_toggle that C-c @ C-c runs). Point moves to the click first, and this runs ahead of the middle-click paste; from a key the command acts at point.

S-mouse-3 moves point to the click and visits the file or URL guessed from the text there; with nothing to guess it reports that and visits nothing. Non-vim presets only, where the right button is not vim's mousemodel button.

vim :debug {cmd} — runs the Ex command under the script debugger. ex_debug (typed.rs:42378) requires the argument (E471 without it) and either hands the command to debug_prompt for the `>` prompt, or, when :debuggreedy is on, executes it reading debug commands from the normal input stream. :debuggreedy / :0debuggreedy are the paired switches.

ex_detach (typed.rs:143) flushes pending writes and raises SIGTSTP, returning the terminal to the controlling shell with the editor stopped in the background; it refuses with 'no controlling shell to return to' when the process is its own session leader. Neovim's :detach detaches a remote UI from a still-running headless server — zmax has no client/server UI protocol, so the editor stops with the terminal rather than continuing headless.
flips vim's `smoothscroll` option and pushes it into the view (zmax_view::view::set_smoothscroll), so a wrapped line scrolls by screen row instead of whole line; reports the new state
SPC T m runs menu_bar_mode, which toggles whether the menu bar is displayed; F10 / M-` still open it
SPC T t runs tool_bar_mode; the state round-trips, and as on a tty in Emacs there is nothing to draw
shows `⏱ H:MM <heading>` in the status line while an org clock runs; org_clock_toggle (org-clock-in/out) starts and stops it, so the construct tracks the real CLOCK line
shows or hides the status line's minor-mode lighter area (Abbrev/Fill/Ovwrt/Fly/Hi/CWarn, plus GG for ggtags and yas for yasnippet)
draws nyan-mode's scroll-position bar (rainbow trail, cat face, outerspace) in the status line; the renderer already existed and had no toggle command

with it on, an optional status-line construct (buffer size, clock, battery, cat, org clock, new-version lighter) is dropped once left+right+its own width would exceed the window; the mandatory elements are never dropped
ggtags-mode: while on, goto_definition resolves the identifier out of the visited etags table (etags_goto_definition) instead of asking a language server, and ` GG` lights in the minor-mode area
yas-minor-mode: while off, try_user_snippet_expand returns early so a snippet key stays ordinary text; ` yas` lights in the minor-mode area while on (on by default)

SPC l is already the sticky Layouts transient state (keymap/vim.rs, `"l" => { "Layouts / LSP" sticky=true`): n/p/C-l/C-h and the digits repeat under bare presses and RET leaves. No code change; the chord had no mapping entry. Evidence cites a leaf inside the state because the report records leaves, not prefixes

opens the pre-filled new-issue URL with the `Emacs last keys` section included; SPC u is a literal chord in zmax rather than a real prefix argument, so this is its own entry point onto the same body builder report_spacemacs_issue uses

the package listing (zmax's Package Menu, paradox's role) opens with list_packages / `:list-packages`. The chord is NOT bound: `SPC a k` is already ai_terminal_command, which port/mapping.json cites for cursor.edit.terminal, so taking it would falsify that entry

switch_to_minibuffer selects the active minibuffer window. The chord is NOT bound: SPC w mirrors vim's C-w window map (enforced by the aliased_modes_are_same_in_default_keymap invariant) where `b` is jump_view_down

view_echo_area_messages opens the *Messages* text in a scratch buffer, not a popup window, and zmax keeps only the current echo-area message rather than a persistent log. The chord is NOT bound: `SPC w p` is rotate_view in the shared SPC w / C-w window map
close_sticky_popup pops the topmost compositor layer (the popup) and errors when only the editor view is up. The chord is NOT bound: `SPC w p` is rotate_view in the shared SPC w / C-w window map
SPC f E now opens the file through `sudo cat` (and saves back through `sudo tee` with :sudo-write); the JetBrains reveal-in-Finder binding that held the key moved to SPC f O

prompts for a library name and reports the file it resolves to, searching ~/.zmax/elpa (top level and one package directory deep) then the config directory; the path is also copied to the clipboard register. Errors with Emacs's `Can't find library:` when nothing matches

runs `:zmax-native update`, which re-resolves and reinstalls every installed zmax plugin from its recorded source (unloading the live cdylib first). Ported to zmax's own package manager rather than ELPA, which zmax has no analogue of

runs `:zmax-native recompile` (new verb): rebuilds every installed plugin from the copy already in the store without re-fetching, dropping the stale cdylib and unloading it first. The zmax equivalent of recompiling elpa
SPC s w g runs helm_google_suggest: fetches Google's suggestion list for the typed query and opens the chosen result in the system browser

`:test-function` runs one named test — the argument, else the identifier under the cursor — through the language's single-test filter (cargo test NAME, pytest -k, go test -run, rspec -e, npm test -- -t, mvn -Dtest=, mix test --only), with the output in the compilation list. The chord is NOT bound: `space m t` is already a leaf twice over (org_todo in the macro, :message-goto-to in the extra table), so `space m t q` cannot resolve
SPC D b p binds the existing ediff_patch_buffer: take a patch from a buffer/file, pick the buffer to apply it to, and review the result side by side. Command existed; the chord did not
SPC D f . diffs zmax's config file against the shipped template, which is the .spacemacs-vs-dotspacemacs-template.el session. Command existed; the chord did not

prompts for two directories and an optional file-name regexp and lists the session group: the names present in both (each mergeable with SPC D m f f) and, separately, the names only one side has. Mirrors the existing SPC D m d 3 with-ancestor command
SPC D m r 3 binds the existing ediff_merge_revisions_with_ancestor (two revisions of this file plus their merge base). Command existed; the chord did not
SPC D m r r binds the existing ediff_merge_revisions (two revisions of this file, no ancestor). Command existed; the chord did not

prints the *Ediff Registry* buffer. Every SPC D session is built through ui::merge::DiffView::new, which now registers its title, so the listing is the real set of sessions started in this run, newest first — Emacs lists live control buffers, zmax lists started sessions

sets ZMAX_STARTUP_TIMING=1 and restarts (refusing on unsaved buffers, like SPC q r), so the next run logs its start-up phase timings. Ported as zmax's own timing instrumentation rather than Emacs's --with-timed-requires, which times `require` calls zmax has none of
smeargle-clear: takes the commit-age tint off. SPC g H became the smeargle prefix; the call-hierarchy command that held the bare key moved to SPC g O

smeargle-commits: ranks the commits that touched the file oldest-first from git blame and paints each visible line's whole-line range with the theme scope for its rank (6 bands), so the oldest and newest commits sit at the ends of the palette; uncommitted lines stay unpainted

smeargle: same painting, but the band is the line's wall-clock age in fixed bands (day, week, month, quarter, year, older), so two files compare against each other. Only the visible line range is turned into ranges each frame

the git README's "use the universal argument SPC u to select a remote repository" for the SPC g l link commands: SPC u SPC g l prompts over `git remote` and records the choice, and current_line_permalink now builds its URL from that remote instead of hardcoding origin

SPC t m M binds the existing toggle_modeline_major_mode, which adds or removes the FileType element (the buffer's language = its major mode here) from the status line. Command existed; the chord did not

shows `⇪<version>` in the status line when a release newer than the running build has been recorded (spacemacs_keys::set_new_version); with nothing recorded the lighter draws nothing even while the toggle is on
sets and clears the `eob:~` item of vim's `fillchars`, which is what draws the rows past the end of the buffer; zmax's renderer already honoured that option and nothing toggled it
SPC T F binds the existing toggle_frame_fullscreen; the frame's fullscreen parameter round-trips, with no visible effect on a tty exactly as in Emacs. Command existed; the chord did not
SPC T M binds the existing toggle_frame_maximized; same tty semantics as SPC T F. Command existed; the chord did not
SPC f e D opens the same config-vs-shipped-template diff SPC D f . opens, which is the ~/.spacemacs vs dotspacemacs-template.el session

opens <config-dir>/init.toml, the file zmax's loader reads before the editor comes up — the early-init.el slot — creating it with a comment header on first use. Ported as zmax's own pre-config rather than Emacs's early-init.el
the finer-grained sibling of SPC q t: restarts with ZMAX_STARTUP_TIMING=advanced so plugin loads are timed alongside the phases. Ported as zmax's timing instrumentation, not Emacs's --adv-timers

log_edit_done finishes the open commit-message buffer and runs the commit, which is the documented behaviour. The chord is NOT bound: zmax's commit buffer is a modal component where every printable key types into the message, so the commit key there is `C-c C-c` (git-commit's own binding, which SPC m c aliases in Spacemacs)
same command as SPC m c (they are two names for one action). The `SPC m ,` chord is NOT bound, for the same reason: the commit buffer is modal and `,` types a comma; `C-c C-c` commits

log_edit_kill_buffer (new) discards the message and closes the commit buffer without committing, erroring when none is open. The chord is NOT bound: the commit buffer is modal and `a` types an `a`; `C-c C-k` aborts there
same command as SPC m a. The chord is NOT bound for the same reason, and `space m k` is separately taken by :message-kill-buffer in the mail draft map

forge-browse-topic: `b` in the forge topic list opens the selected issue/PR's URL in the system browser. Spacemacs's SPC m is the major-mode leader; in zmax the topic list is a modal component that owns its keys, so the letter lives in that map
forge-checkout-pullreq: `C` runs `gh pr checkout <n>` on the selected topic, and says so when the topic is an issue rather than a pull request
forge-toggle-draft: `d` flips the selected pull request between draft and ready via `gh pr ready` / `gh pr ready --undo`, refusing on issues

forge-delete-comment: `D` inside a topic's post list deletes the post under the cursor (`gh api -X DELETE .../issues/comments/<id>`), asking for a second `D` to confirm; the opening post cannot be deleted, matching forge
forge-edit-post: `e` opens the multi-line body editor over the selected topic, pre-filled with its current body

forge-edit-topic-marks: `m` edits the topic's marks. A mark is forge's unshared label, so zmax keeps them in .git/zmax-forge-marks.json (alongside the personal notes) and never sends them to the forge; a name typed here that is not a known mark yet is added. Server-side labels moved to `l`
forge-create-mark: `M` prompts for a name and adds it to the repo's known-mark list without putting it on a topic
forge-edit-topic-note: `n` edits the topic's personal note, which forge keeps locally; zmax stores it in .git/zmax-forge-notes.json
forge-edit-topic-review-requests: `r` reads comma-separated logins and runs `gh pr edit <n> --add-reviewer`, refusing on issues
forge-edit-topic-state: `s` reads open/closed/draft/ready and runs the matching gh verb (issue|pr reopen / close, pr ready [--undo]), then re-reads the list; an unknown word is refused by name
forge-edit-topic-title: `t` opens the title pre-filled and runs `gh issue|pr edit <n> --title` when it changes
forge-copy-url-at-point-as-kill: `u` pushes the selected topic's web URL onto the kill ring
the item's name is a truncated `SPC T ~`; same binding as spacemacs.keybinding.spc_tU_tilde — sets/clears `fillchars` `eob:~`, which draws the ~ on the rows past the end of the buffer

prompts for a face — zmax's faces are the active theme's scopes — and shows its resolved foreground, background, attributes and underline in a *Help*-style scratch buffer, naming the theme and the `:highlight` line that changes it. An unknown name is refused

help_go_forward steps forward through the Help browser's history (the counterpart of `g b`, which is bound). The chord is NOT bound: `g f` is vim's goto-file in zmax, the same reason the existing comment in keymap/vim.rs gives for `g b` taking only the back half

help_follow_symbol (new) takes the identifier under the cursor and opens the Help browser filtered to it, erroring when there is no symbol at point. The chord is NOT bound: `g h` is vim's Select-mode entry in zmax
SPC h I opens the pre-filled new-issue URL (description / reproduction sections plus a System Info block). Command existed; the chord did not

paradox's `f` filter prefix now arms the package menu's filter map alongside `/`, so `f k` reads a keyword and narrows the listing to the packages carrying it — the same filter package_menu_filter_by_keyword applies

`f r` (and `/ r`) reads a regexp and keeps the packages whose name or summary matches it — a new Filter::Regexp in zmax_core::package, since the other filters all match a substring. An unparseable regexp matches nothing rather than everything
`f u` applies the upgradable filter with no prompt, leaving only installed packages with a newer version available — the same filter package_menu_filter_upgradable applies

`S P` in the package menu sorts by package name; the key already worked and had no command to cite, so the sort now goes through PackageMenuView::sort_by, which both the key and package_menu_sort_by_name call. A second press reverses the order (tabulated-list-sort)
`S S` sorts by status in package.el's order (available, installed, external, obsolete), ties broken by name; a second press reverses it

`S *` sorts by paradox's GitHub-star column. zmax carries no star count per row, so every package ties and the sort falls through to the name predicate — which is what paradox itself shows before its async star fetch fills in
SPC F d deletes the displayed frame (refusing when it is the only one). The fzf `:Todo` binding that squatted on the key moved to SPC F x
SPC F o cycles focus to the next frame, wrapping. The fzf `:Locate` binding that squatted on the key moved to SPC F u

doc-view-toggle-display: `C-c C-c` in the DocView overlay leaves the rendered page and shows the document buffer's text again (`:doc-view` renders it back); `C-c C-t` in the same prefix is doc-view-open-text. The evidence is the `C-c` prefix because the report's component-keymap scanner records the prefix key, not the two-key chord
SPC K r l binds the existing kmacro_call_ring_2nd (run the second macro in the ring). Command existed; the chord did not
SPC p I runs :projectile-invalidate-cache. zmax's file picker walks the project fresh on every open, so there is no cached listing to purge and the command reports the invalidation projectile reports

SPC p T runs :projectile-test-project — the project's test command from the project root, remembered per root, with the output in the compilation list. The command existed; the chord was taken by an fzf `:Todo` binding, which moved to SPC F x
C-h C-\ now runs set_input_method (Select Input Method), the help-map alias of the C-x RET C-\ binding

the C-x 8 prefix is live and inserts characters: `C-x 8 e` and `C-x 8 RET` open the Unicode picker (insert-char). It is a prefix, so the evidence cites one of its leaves — the report records leaves, not prefixes. No code change needed for this item
C-x RET C-\ now runs set_input_method, which prompts for the input method the buffer composes characters with; it sits with the rest of the C-x RET coding-system map

sends XMPP messages to a JID or a MUC room through the sendxmpp binary, reading credentials from ~/.sendxmpprc, and lists the configured JIDs (never the passwords). jabber.el's roster buffer, presence, subscription requests and MUC join need a persistent authenticated XMPP session, which these one-shot commands do not hold, so those are absent.

:unicode-fonts prints a sample sheet of 34 Unicode blocks with the display width zmax computes for each row, and :unicode-fonts-char reports a character's codepoint, block and width. The per-block font assignment and the ligature setup that unicode-fonts.el does are not ported: a terminal application cannot choose a font per Unicode block, that is the emulator's fallback chain, so the sheet reports coverage rather than configuring it.

plays a typewriter click on every key the editor reads and a bell on Return. The two samples are synthesised once into ~/.cache/zmax/selectric (25 ms of decaying noise; a 1 kHz decaying tone for the return) and played detached with afplay/paplay/aplay/play; turning the mode on errors if none of those is installed. Sounds are rate-limited to one per 35 ms so a held key does not fork a player per repeat.

fetches a strip from xkcd.com's info.0.json API, caches the image under ~/.cache/zmax/xkcd, draws it with the terminal image viewer chain and shows title, date, alt text and transcript in a scratch buffer. next/prev step the last-shown number, random picks one in 1..=latest, and the two open commands launch the strip page and its explainxkcd page in the browser.

the conversion half works: the region is rewritten through opencc (t2s.json / s2t.json), falling back to cconv, which is the layer's documented chinese-conv-backend; :youdao-lookup queries dict.youdao.com's JSON API; :chinese-pinyin reports readings through the pinyin binary. The pyim/wubi input methods, the fcitx auto-switch on leaving insert state, find-by-pinyin-dired and ace-pinyin are not ported.

romaji-to-hiragana conversion is complete (gojuon, dakuten/handakuten, youon digraphs, sokuon from a doubled consonant, n/nn), and the kana/katakana commands are the U+3040 to U+30A0 codepoint shift; :migemo-search runs cmigemo to turn romaji into a Japanese-matching regex. SKK's kanji conversion needs a jisyo dictionary and an interactive candidate loop, and the japanese-holidays calendar is not ported.

all four alda-mode playback commands: the buffer plays with `alda play --file`, and region/block/line play with `alda play --history <text before the region> --code <text>` so earlier part and octave declarations still apply. Each first runs `alda status` and starts `alda server` when the output says the server is down, matching alda-run-cmd. languages.toml already carries the .alda entry (comment token, indent).

connects to a running Extempore process over TCP (localhost:7099 by default, overridable per call or by $EXTEMPORE_HOST/$EXTEMPORE_PORT) and writes s-expressions to it, which is exactly what extempore-mode's open-network-stream eval path does; :extempore-run starts the binary from $EXTEMPORE_PATH. Each send opens its own connection rather than holding emacs' persistent socket, so a reply arriving later than 250 ms is missed. .xtm files already resolve to the scheme entry in languages.toml.

runs a .factor file, evaluates source with `factor -e=`, starts the UI listener with the layer's own `fuel-start-remote-listener*` command line, and lists a vocabulary's words. The FUEL wire session is not ported, so everything that needs it is absent: the seven refactorings, fuel-update-usings, fuel-help, apropos, callers/callees, edit-word-at-point, stack-effect inference and both scaffolders. languages.toml carries the grammarless .factor entry.

the upstream layer is jr-mode and nothing else - a major mode claiming .jr with highlighting, no commands and no variables. languages.toml gains a jr entry (file type, // and /* */ comment tokens, 4-space indent, JR being Java plus concurrency keywords) and :jr-mode sets the buffer's language the way M-x jr-mode does. Grammarless: no tree-sitter parser and no language server for JR exist.

the upstream layer is kivy-mode and nothing else. languages.toml already carries the .kv entry (# comments, 4-space indent per the Kivy docs) and :kivy-mode sets the buffer's language. No language server for the kv language exists.

both commands the layer binds: :mercury-compile runs `mmc --make <module>` in the file's directory with the module name taken from the file stem, and :mercury-run compiles then runs ./<module>, reporting a compile failure as the error. languages.toml carries the mercury entry (% and /* */ comments, 4-space indent per the project's coding standard).

languages.toml gains an octave entry - the matlab tree-sitter grammar (Octave and MATLAB share it, and .m keeps resolving to matlab), Octave's own # comment and #{ #} block tokens, the octave/octave-cli shebangs, .octaverc and .oct file types, and the octave-lsp language server. The send commands run through `octave --no-gui --quiet --eval`, and help/lookfor query the same way. Partial because that is batch execution: unlike inferior-octave, variables and pkg load do not persist between two calls.

Raku's file types used to sit on the perl entry, which gave a .raku file perl's grammar, perl's language server and perl's indent width. languages.toml now has its own raku entry: the acrion/tree-sitter-raku grammar, # and #`( ) comment tokens, 4-space indent, the raku/rakudo/perl6 shebangs, and the raku-language-server (zef install Raku::LanguageServer). The grammar is a Raku-patched fork of tree-sitter-perl, so runtime/queries/raku/*.scm inherit perl's queries rather than duplicating them.

the powershell half gains the PowerShell Editor Services language server (pwsh -Command 'Import-Module PowerShellEditorServices; Start-EditorServices -Stdio'; the module ships only as a GitHub release zip, so languages.toml documents putting its module directory on $PSModulePath) plus :powershell-run/:powershell-eval and powershell.el's regexp-to-regex rewrite ported from its source. The batch half gains the wharflab tree-sitter-batch grammar with its highlights query, and bat-mode's bat-run, bat-cmd-help and bat-template; :bat-labels is bmx-mode's label navigation as a table of definitions and references. Running a .bat needs Windows or wine, and says so.

the region (or current line) goes to the clipboard wrapped in another platform's code markup, with every format from copy-as-format's own alist. The layer's SPC x f chords are bound to the matching command.
:denote creates a timestamped IDENTIFIER--title__keywords.org note under ~/Documents/notes and opens it; :denote-link inserts a link to another note by its identifier.
downloads and opens an IETF document named by the argument or the word under the cursor (rfc2119, draft-..., std66), caching it so a second open is local; a `!` argument re-downloads.

highlights the line the cursor landed on for 400 ms after a jump, then repaints to clear it. Emacs advises a list of navigation commands; zmax detects the jump in the render path instead - a cursor move of more than one line in a frame - which covers searches, goto-line, xref and window switches and deliberately does not fire for j/k stepping, the distinction nav-flash-exclude-commands exists to draw.

parinfer's three modes over the buffer, applied on switch: indent mode infers the trailing close-parens from indentation, paren mode re-indents to match the existing parens, and smart mode runs indent mode but falls back to paren mode when the change would alter brackets on the cursor line. Strings, character literals and comments are inert, all three bracket kinds are handled, and a mismatched bracket is reported without touching the text. SPC t P flips smart <-> paren, as the layer documents.

keeps one pianobar child alive with piped stdin and a reader thread draining its output into a 500-line ring buffer, and writes the control character the layer's binding sends (p, n, +, -, t, s, i, q). Every command auto-starts pianobar; :pianobar-output pages what it printed. The chords are not bound because SPC a m is already a leaf in zmax's keymap.

playback control of the desktop client through AppleScript on macOS and playerctl (or dbus-send to org.mpris.MediaPlayer2.spotify) on Linux, plus Web API search for tracks, albums and artists using a client-credentials token from $SPOTIFY_CLIENT_ID/$SPOTIFY_CLIENT_SECRET. The chords are not bound because SPC a m is already a leaf in zmax's keymap.

keeps one ghci child alive (or `cabal exec ghci`), boots it with BootTidal.hs via :script the way tidal.el does, and sends the block around the cursor wrapped in :{ ... :}. :tidal-run-orbit sends the block as d1..d9, :tidal-stop-orbit sends upstream's `mapM_ ($ silence) [dN]`, and :tidal-hush silences everything. Sound still comes from SuperCollider/SuperDirt running outside the editor, as it does under emacs.

looks a term up in Dash on macOS (`open -g dash-plugin://query=...`, or keys=<docset>&query=... for the docset-restricted form) and in Zeal elsewhere (`zeal --query`), erroring by name when neither is installed. :dash-docsets lists what is installed by reading Dash's DocSets directory or Zeal's docsets directory.

the text side of djvu.el over djvulibre: djvutxt for a document's or a page's text, `djvused -e n` for the page count, `djvused -e print-outline` for the outline, a page-by-page search that reports `page N: <line>` (djvu-occur), and ddjvu to render one page to an image file. The image reading mode, the invert/dark mode and the mouse-drawn annotations (highlights, text notes, pushpins, lines, arrows) are not ported.

reads the feed list from ~/.config/zmax/elfeed-feeds (one URL per line with optional tags, created with a commented example when missing), fetches each feed, parses both RSS 2.0 and Atom, and pages the entries newest first with their dates and links; an argument filters by tag or by a substring of the title. :elfeed-show fetches one entry's page and strips it to text.

spray's RSVP display: one word at a time, held at a spray-wpm-paced tick with the optimal-recognition-point letter accented, pausing longer for long words and for sentence punctuation. Space pauses, h/l step a word, f/s change the speed, q quits.

one command per p4.el operation the layer's SPC p 4 table lists, each shelling out to the p4 client and paging its output; :p4 runs any other p4 subcommand. Environment (P4PORT/P4CLIENT/P4USER) is the client's, as under emacs.

all four features. rainbow-mode paints colour literals with the colour they name (3/6/9/12-digit hex, rgb()/rgba()/hsl()/hsla(), and the 148 CSS colour names) using an interned RGB face. rainbow-identifiers colours every identifier from its own text by rainbow-identifiers.el's CIE L*a*b* chooser - hash to an angle on a circle of radius `saturation` at plane `lightness`, converted to sRGB - with SHA-2 in place of upstream's SHA-1. color-identifiers restricts that to words the tree-sitter grammar calls an identifier or variable. Both have a global variant, and SPC C i s / SPC C i l raise, lower or reset the two knobs. The SPC t C a/v chords are unbound because SPC t C is already zmax's superword toggle.

the layer is apache-mode and nothing else: editing support for httpd.conf, .htaccess and vhost files. languages.toml carries the apache entry (file types including the httpd/conf glob, # comments, 4-space indent per cfengine-indent's sibling default) and :apache-mode sets the buffer's language the way M-x apache-mode does. Grammarless and serverless: no tree-sitter parser and no language server for httpd configuration exist.

languages.toml carries the cfengine entry (.cf, # comments, the 2-space step cfengine-indent defaults to) and :cfengine-mode sets the buffer's language, which is cfengine3-mode's editing support. The flycheck syntax checking, company completion and the ob-cfengine3 babel block execution are not ported, and no tree-sitter parser or language server for the CFEngine DSL exists.

edit-server.el's protocol: :edit-server-start binds 127.0.0.1:9292 and queues each POST from the Chrome 'Edit with Emacs' extension with its connection held open, :edit-server-take opens a queued body in a buffer, and :edit-server-finish answers that connection with the buffer's text so the browser textarea updates. The flymd live markdown preview half of the layer is not ported.

conda activation is a shell function, so it is ported the way it has to work for a long-lived process: the env prefix is resolved from `conda env list`, then CONDA_PREFIX/CONDA_DEFAULT_ENV are set and <prefix>/bin is prepended to this process's PATH, so every later subprocess - language servers, the terminal, run configurations - sees the environment. Deactivating restores the saved PATH.

sends queries to a cluster over its HTTP API ($ES_URL, default localhost:9200): cluster health, _cat/indices, _cat/nodes, a Lucene query against one index rendered as _id/_score/_source lines, and :es-request for an arbitrary METHOD path body - es-mode's 'send the query under point'. PUT is sent as POST, which is correct for search and aggregation endpoints but not for index creation.

the weather half of the layer: a 5-day/3-hour forecast from OpenWeatherMap when $OPENWEATHER_API_KEY is set and from wttr.in (no key needed) otherwise, with the status line naming which source answered, plus a one-line current-conditions form. :sun-times reports sunrise, sunset, solar noon and day length in UTC from sunrise-sunset.org. theme-changer's automatic light/dark switch at sunrise and sunset, and osx-location's CoreLocation coordinate updates, are not ported.

talks to a Jupyter server's REST API ($JUPYTER_URL, $JUPYTER_TOKEN): lists notebooks, renders one as text with a # In[n]: header per cell plus its source and text output, and lists, starts and stops kernels. Executing a cell is not ported and no command pretends to: Jupyter has no execute endpoint on the REST API - execution goes over the kernel's websocket channel, and zmax has no websocket client.

the layer exists so other layers get a working node execution path. :nvm-list reads the versions installed under $NVM_DIR, :nvm-use puts one on this process's PATH so every later subprocess (language servers, the terminal, run configurations) uses it and reports the resolved `node --version`, and the two npm commands list and run package.json scripts.

one command per entry in the layer's SPC a t P table, each driving the pass binary: list the tree, copy a password to the clipboard for 45 s, show, generate, insert a multi-line entry over stdin, rename, remove, init, and the three password-store-otp operations. :pass-edit shows the entry rather than opening $EDITOR, which a one-shot command cannot host.

services are declared in ~/.config/zmax/prodigy.json (name, command, args, cwd, tags, url), which is written with an example on first use because there is no lisp reader here. :prodigy lists them with their running state and takes a name-or-tag filter (prodigy's f n / f t), and the others start a service detached, stop it with SIGTERM, restart it, and report its URL.

quickurl.el's named-URL store, kept in ~/.quickurls as name<TAB>url (a two-column file rather than a lisp alist). :quickurl-list pages the store, :quickurl-add stores or replaces a name, :quickurl looks one up, and :quickurl-browse opens it.

rebox2's box drawing and reshaping with its numeric style codes: 85 templates ported from rebox2's registry (32 generic, 20 text-mode, 21 C, plus the 12 the layer registers itself), style detection by rebox-guess-style's heaviest-match rule, unbox, style cycling over the layer's (71 72 73) loop, centring and horizontal shifting. Boxes are padded so every line of a frame is the same width; the comment token comes from the buffer's language.

the three sailfish-scratchbox operations: `mb2 build` in the project, installing the built RPMs into the Scratchbox 2 target named by $SAILFISH_SB2_TARGET, and scp-ing them to the device named by $SAILFISH_DEVICE. Both variables are named in the error when unset.

speaks the Transmission RPC protocol to a running daemon, including the X-Transmission-Session-Id 409 handshake and Basic auth from $TRANSMISSION_RPC_AUTH: the torrent list with status, progress and rates, add by magnet/URL/path, remove with or without data, start/stop/verify, relocate, the global speed limits, turtle mode, and the per-torrent file and peer listings. The queue reordering (J/K/H/L), marking, labels, per-torrent priorities and the turtle schedule are not ported.

one command per box operation in the layer's SPC a t v table, each running the vagrant binary in the project and paging its output. vagrant-tramp's interactive box shell is not ported - :vagrant-ssh prints `vagrant ssh-config` instead, since a one-shot command cannot host the session - and editing files at /vagrant:box:path is absent.

draws vim's ~ markers on the rows past the end of the buffer, as buffer text rather than a fringe bitmap - which is the whole point of the package. zmax already renders those rows from vim's fillchars eob: item; the mode is the toggle the layer's t~ binding drives, consulted when fillchars names no eob item.

the ox-confluence half is complete: :confluence-export converts the region or buffer from markdown/org to Confluence wiki markup (headings to h1..h6, bold/italic, fenced code to {code:lang}, inline code to {{...}}, lists, links and table header rows). :confluence-page and :confluence-search read pages and run CQL searches over the REST API with Basic auth from $CONFLUENCE_AUTH. Saving a buffer back to the server as a minor or major edit is not ported.

one command per chord in the layer's SPC a w e table, each driving the geeknote CLI - find by keyword, show, create with a title and content, remove, move to another notebook - plus a notebook listing.

fetches a feed's ids from the Hacker News Firebase API and then each item, paging them numbered with score, comment count, author, the story URL and the HN comments URL. The feed (top/new/best/ask/show/job) and the count are arguments. :hackernews-item shows one story with its top-level comments, HTML-unescaped and tag-stripped.
fetches lobste.rs' hottest.json or newest.json and pages the stories numbered with their tags, score, comment count, submitter, and both the story and comment URLs.

reddigg's three views over Reddit's public JSON endpoints: one subreddit's listing (sort and limit are arguments), the hot listing of every subreddit in ~/.config/zmax/reddit-subs under per-subreddit headings, and a post's comment tree rendered depth-first and indented two spaces per level.

engine-mode's engine table (26 engines: google, duckduckgo, github, gitlab, stackoverflow, wikipedia, youtube, amazon with its configurable TLD, docs.rs, crates.io, mdn, npm, the Arch wiki, wolfram-alpha, and the rest) as URL templates. :search-engine builds the URL for an engine and query and opens it in the browser; an unknown engine errors with the nearest names. :search-engines pages the table.

hands a stream URL to the streamlink binary at the requested quality (default best), spawned detached so the player outlives the command, and reports the pid. :streamlink-qualities lists the stream names streamlink offers for a URL.

searches live channels and lists the top live streams over the Twitch Helix API using $TWITCH_CLIENT_ID and $TWITCH_OAUTH_TOKEN (both named in the error when unset), resolving a game name to its game_id when one is given, and :twitch-open opens a channel in the browser. Opening a stream in a player is the streamlink layer's :streamlink; the ERC chat connection is not ported.

the timeline, a user's tweets, recent search and posting, over the Twitter/X API v2 with $TWITTER_BEARER_TOKEN (named in the error when unset). Partial because the endpoints behind these require a paid API tier and answer 403 otherwise, and because the transient state's per-tweet operations from twittering-mode - favourite, retweet, follow, direct message, delete - are not ported.

reports today's coding time from the wakatime CLI, sends a heartbeat for a file, pages per-language and per-project totals for a range from the WakaTime API using $WAKATIME_API_KEY, and opens the dashboard in the browser. Partial because heartbeats are sent on request rather than automatically on every save and edit the way wakatime-mode hooks them.

transcribes locally with whisper.cpp: :whisper-file normalises the input to 16 kHz mono wav with ffmpeg when needed and runs the whisper binary with the selected model and language, :whisper-record captures from the default microphone (avfoundation on macOS, alsa on Linux) for a number of seconds and transcribes that, and the two selection commands set or list the model and language for the session.
